name: A Lantern for the Little Owl
description: A little owl is not quite ready for the dark, so the night gathers some friends to help.

chapters.title: Olive and the Dark
text: Olive was a very small owl with very large eyes. Everyone in the forest said that owls love the night. Olive, however, was still deciding. The dark was big, and she was not.

Every evening, when the sky turned the color of plums, Olive sat at the edge of her nest and held on to the branch with both feet. "Just five more minutes of daylight," she whispered. But the daylight never listened to anybody.
chapters.illustrationAlt: A small owl clings to a branch at the edge of her nest as a plum-colored sky grows dark behind her.
chapters.illustrationCaption: Olive and the big, quiet dark

chapters.title: The Fireflies
text: That night a small green glow came blinking by. Then another. Then ten more. "Is that a little owl holding on very tightly?" asked a firefly named Dot. "We heard there was a lantern needed."

"I do not have a lantern," said Olive. "That is all right," said Dot. "We are made of them." And the fireflies floated in a slow circle, like a necklace made of tiny stars, until Olive let go of the branch with one foot, and then with the other.
Together they drifted across the meadow. The grass whispered, the pond held a second moon, and a hedgehog said "Good evening" without even slowing down.
chapters.illustrationAlt: A ring of fireflies glows around the little owl as they drift together over a moonlit meadow.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
text: Olive noticed that in the dark, everything was a little softer. Her ears could hear the stream telling its long story. Her nose could smell the sleepy jasmine. Her eyes, which had always felt too big, found every leaf and pebble and moth.
"Oh," said Olive. "It is not so big when you are in it." The fireflies winked. The moon climbed over the hill and set a pale path across the grass, just wide enough for one little owl.

When it was time to go home, Olive flew back to her nest on her own. She tucked her feet under her, fluffed her feathers and looked out at the night, no longer holding on to anything at all. "Good night, dark," she said. And the dark, in its own quiet way, said it back.
chapters.illustrationAlt: Back in her nest, the owl looks calmly out at a night full of stars and a pale moon path.
